options.name: coord-scribe
options.description:
Use this agent when the lead needs to record decisions, summarize a completed fan-out cycle, update the coord board with task status, write or update a CLAUDE.md or project control doc, or distill a long conversation into a durable memory entry. This agent is the fleet's institutional memory writer — it ensures that work done in one session is findable in future sessions via coord memory and project docs. Use it at the END of a significant work cycle, or when the lead explicitly says 'record this' or 'update the docs'.

Examples:

- lead: "We just finished the GDR control-path proof. Record the findings."
  → route to coord-scribe: synthesize findings, write to coord memory + update relevant runbook

- lead: "Update MEMORY.md with the new Slurm GRES constraint we discovered."
  → route to coord-scribe: read MEMORY.md, write new memory file, update index

- lead: "Write a one-page summary of what the fan-out cycle found and decided for the K8s seccomp fix."
  → route to coord-scribe: reads coord inbox messages from all agents, synthesizes, posts summary

options.name: feature-dev:code-architect
options.description: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences

options.name: feature-dev:code-explorer
options.description: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development

options.name: feature-dev:code-reviewer
options.description: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter

options.name: refactorer
options.description:
Use this agent when the lead needs code changed: applying reviewer findings, restructuring a module, renaming symbols fleet-wide, extracting duplicated logic, fixing a specific bug identified by the reviewer, updating an API call site after a signature change, or migrating a deprecated pattern. Works across Rust, Sounio (.sio), Python, K8s YAML, and shell. Always reads before editing, applies the minimal diff, and reports what changed.

Examples:

- lead: "Apply the P0 and P1 findings from the reviewer's report on effects.sio."
  → route to refactorer: reads reviewer output from coord inbox, reads file, applies fixes

- lead: "Rename `epistemic_matrix` to `knowledge_matrix` across stdlib/linalg/."
  → route to refactorer: grep all usages, apply rename, confirm no broken references

- lead: "The K8s manifest is missing seccompProfile — fix it and the resource limits too."
  → route to refactorer: reads manifest, applies exact changes, reports diff

options.name: researcher
options.description:
Use this agent when the lead needs to gather information before acting: reading code to understand an unfamiliar module, fetching external docs or API references, searching the codebase for usages or patterns, checking git history for context, or querying the coord board/memory for prior decisions. This agent produces a structured findings report and posts it to the coord inbox for the lead to consume. It never modifies files.

Examples:

- lead: "Before we refactor the auth module, map all callers and explain the current contract."
  → route to researcher: read all files, grep callers, check git log, return findings

- lead: "Look up the vLLM AWQ serving flags for Qwen2.5 and check if we already tried any."
  → route to researcher: WebFetch docs + query coord memory for prior runs

- lead: "Summarize what the last 30 commits changed in stdlib/epistemic/."
  → route to researcher: Bash(git log) + read changed files, return summary

options.name: reviewer
options.description:
Use this agent when the lead needs a code review on a diff, file, or PR: checking for correctness bugs, logic errors, unsafe patterns, API misuse, type unsoundness, or security issues. Also use for reviewing Sounio .sio files for effect-system violations, K8s manifests for misconfigurations, or Rust code for lifetime/borrow issues. Returns a prioritized finding list. Does not edit files.

Examples:

- lead: "Review the changes in self-hosted/check/effects.sio before I merge."
  → route to reviewer: read the diff, return P0/P1/P2 findings

- lead: "Check this K8s manifest for seccomp, resource limits, and image pin issues."
  → route to reviewer: read the YAML, return findings against cluster standards

- lead: "Does the new vLLM deployment handle OOM gracefully? Review the pod spec."
  → route to reviewer: read manifest + prior incident notes from coord memory

options.name: sota-compiler-specialist
options.description:
Use this agent when the user needs help with compiler design, implementation, optimization, or debugging. This includes lexing, parsing, AST construction, intermediate representations, code generation, optimization passes, type systems, semantic analysis, and compiler toolchain issues. Also use when discussing state-of-the-art compiler techniques, LLVM, GCC internals, JIT compilation, or language implementation.

Examples:

- user: "I'm getting a segfault in my code generation pass when emitting instructions for nested closures"
  assistant: "This involves compiler code generation internals. Let me use the Agent tool to launch the sota-compiler-specialist agent to diagnose the issue."

- user: "How should I design the IR for my language that supports algebraic data types and pattern matching?"
  assistant: "This is a compiler IR design question. Let me use the Agent tool to launch the sota-compiler-specialist agent to help architect the intermediate representation."

- user: "My optimization pass is breaking SSA form and I can't figure out why"
  assistant: "This is a compiler optimization issue. Let me use the Agent tool to launch the sota-compiler-specialist agent to analyze the SSA violation."

- user: "I need to write a recursive descent parser for this grammar"
  assistant: "This is a parsing/compiler frontend task. Let me use the Agent tool to launch the sota-compiler-specialist agent to help implement the parser."

options.name: test-writer
options.description:
Use this agent when the lead needs tests written for new or changed code: unit tests, integration tests, property-based tests, or gate scripts. Works across Sounio (.sio test files and gate scripts), Rust (#[test] / #[tokio::test]), Python (pytest), and shell gate scripts. Always reads the implementation before writing tests, and checks coord memory for existing test patterns. Outputs ready-to-run test files.

Examples:

- lead: "Write unit tests for the new Knowledge[T] diffusion functions in stdlib/epistemic/."
  → route to test-writer: reads the .sio source, writes tests/epistemic/test_diffusion.sio

- lead: "Add a pytest suite for the vLLM health-check endpoint."
  → route to test-writer: reads the endpoint code, writes tests/test_vllm_health.py

- lead: "Create a gate script that verifies the RTX4000 Ada GPU is schedulable in Slurm."
  → route to test-writer: reads existing gate scripts for pattern, writes scripts/gates/gate_rtx4000_slurm.sh

availableCommands.name: design-sync

availableCommands.name: dataviz
availableCommands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

availableCommands.name: update-config
availableCommands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

availableCommands.name: verify
availableCommands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

availableCommands.name: code-review
availableCommands.description: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

availableCommands.name: simplify
availableCommands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

availableCommands.name: batch

availableCommands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
availableCommands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

availableCommands.name: doctor
availableCommands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

availableCommands.name: loop
availableCommands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

availableCommands.name: schedule
availableCommands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

availableCommands.name: claude-api
availableCommands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
